name: face-rating
title: Face Rating
description: A five-level feedback rating built around one large line-drawn face. Hovering a number previews that mood as the mouth, eyes, brows and colour spring to it, and clicking commits the rating with a small bounce.
use: A product asks for a quick 1-5 satisfaction score and wants the mood to be visible, not just stars.
avoid: Five coarse levels suit satisfaction, not a precise score, and the face needs a clear question beside it.
a11y: A labelled radio group with arrow-key movement, per-level aria labels and reduced-motion support; the face is aria-hidden. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A dark rounded card holds a question, a grey subtitle and a big circular line-art face with two dot eyes and a curved mouth. Under it sit five small round number buttons and a centred mood word; the face's outline and features change colour from grey to rose, orange, amber, lime or emerald with the level.
behaves: Hovering any of the five numbers previews that mood: the mouth curve, eye shape, eyebrows and stroke colour spring to the level and a mood label crossfades in. Clicking commits it with a quick bounce, arrow keys move through the group, and the footer confirms the saved score.
customise: Value or defaultValue, mood labels, the group label, showLabel and size are props; the five mood colours and the mouth geometry are constants in the file.
weight: light: One small SVG face and five buttons with spring morphs on hover.
demo: Question 'How was your onboarding call?', a subtitle about Maya the success manager, and moods from Terrible to Amazing.
issues: Mood is carried mostly by colour, which colour-blind users may not distinguish.
The five number buttons are much smaller than the face, so the control feels disconnected from its options.
polishWhy: Expressive, friendly face morph with solid radio semantics; colour does most of the mood work.
usage:
